bullets.text: Hoax bomb threats have targeted European airlines and airports for the second time in a week, affecting at least 21 flights across Europe.
Paraguay's President Santiago Peña resigned following a bank collapse and a vote in the lower house of congress to pursue an impeachment trial against him.
French protests have seen a surge in numbers as unions joined strikes over the high cost of living, with estimates of participants ranging from 600,000 to much higher figures.
The Western Australian government has agreed with a mining company to scrap an Indigenous heritage zone, leading to a court challenge from traditional owners.
One Nation is reportedly asking donors at a Sydney fundraiser to sign non-disclosure agreements, raising transparency concerns ahead of the NSW election.
Pauline Hanson will appeal a racial discrimination ruling in the High Court, following a previous ruling against her.

The Nasdaq and S&P 500 experienced significant plunges, with chip stocks and other technology shares falling sharply. This market reaction is attributed to investor fears that a 'blue wave' of newly elected Democrats in the US midterms will lead to increased scrutiny and potential regulation of the artificial intelligence industry, slowing data center development.

The tech industry is facing a growing backlash against its expansion and power, leading some executives to admit the industry has fueled hostility towards its own growth. This sentiment, coupled with the Democratic success in the midterms, threatens the projected trillion-dollar data center boom.

China's banking system is grappling with the hangover from years of 'Wild East capitalism,' as indebted tycoons pose a significant risk to lenders. Meanwhile, China's AI stock market struggles are seen as a warning sign of what happens when the supply of new technology catches up with demand.
